unit.title: Ratios, Rates & Proportional Reasoning
unit.essential_question: How do constant multiplicative relationships help us compare, predict, scale, and make fair decisions?
big_ideas: A ratio describes a multiplicative comparison between quantities.
Equivalent ratios, tables, and double number lines organize one ratio family.
A unit rate creates a fair per-one comparison.
Proportional relationships share a constant of proportionality and have equations y=kx.
Scale and conversion models are trustworthy only when units and assumptions are explicit.
unit.architecture: Integrated Grade 9 learning: instruction + reasoning + practice + application + tools + reflection + mastery

lessons.title: Ratio Meaning, Language & Equivalent Ratios
objectives: Interpret part-to-part and part-to-whole ratios.
Write ratios in words, colon, and fraction notation.
Generate equivalent ratios by scaling both terms.
Distinguish multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.

lessons.title: Ratio Tables & Double Number Lines
objectives: Build and interpret ratio tables.
Use double number lines to show corresponding quantities.
Find missing values through scaling and decomposition.
Explain why equivalent pairs lie in one ratio family.

lessons.title: Rates, Unit Rates & Fair Comparisons
objectives: Interpret rates with units.
Calculate unit rates and unit prices.
Compare options using a common unit.
Use estimation to judge whether a unit rate is reasonable.

lessons.title: Proportional Relationships in Tables, Graphs & Equations
objectives: Identify the constant of proportionality.
Write proportional equations in the form y=kx.
Graph proportional relationships through the origin.
Interpret points and slopes as paired quantities and unit rates.

lessons.title: Solving Proportions & Direct Variation
objectives: Solve proportions using scaling, unit rates, or cross products.
Write and use direct-variation equations.
Check solutions by substitution and estimation.
Choose a strategy suited to the numbers and context.

lessons.title: Scale Drawings, Maps & Similar Figures
objectives: Interpret map and drawing scales.
Use scale factors to find actual and represented lengths.
Solve missing-side problems in similar figures.
Check that units are compatible before calculating.

lessons.title: Proportional vs Nonproportional Relationships
objectives: Test tables, graphs, equations, and contexts for proportionality.
Distinguish multiplicative from additive relationships.
Interpret a nonzero intercept as a starting amount.
Explain why a constant difference is not the same as a constant ratio.

lessons.title: Conversions & Multi-Step Proportional Modelling
objectives: Use conversion factors and dimensional analysis.
Solve multi-step rate and proportion problems.
Compare models and communicate assumptions.
Evaluate whether proportional reasoning is appropriate for a context.

practice.title: Foundation Practice
practice.description: Scaffolded ratio models, tables, unit-rate support, and guided steps.

practice.title: Core Practice
practice.description: Complete unit-level practice across ratios, rates, proportional equations, scale, and modelling.

practice.title: Extended Practice
practice.description: Proof, error analysis, precision, model comparison, and unfamiliar proportional situations.
